text.en: Six-year-old Rakesh eats sweet-sour cherries in the Mussoorie bazaar and wonders what to do with the seed.

Rakesh, aged six, walks home from the Mussoorie bazaar eating cherries that came all the way from the Kashmir Valley.
In the Himalayan foothills where he lives there are few fruit trees because the soil is stony and the climate is dry.
He asks his grandfather whether cherry seeds are lucky, and Grandfather says nothing is lucky if you put it away, you must put it to use.
Grandfather tells him to plant the seed, and Rakesh digs a place in a shady corner where it will not be disturbed.
Planting a seed teaches patience and care: the plant needs water, protection and time.
The story is about growing a tree and about the bond between a child, his grandfather and nature.
The theme of the story is that small actions, like planting a seed, can bring lasting joy.
Words: tang is a strong sharp taste, and sown means planted by scattering seeds.
The narrator uses sensory details like sweet and sour, small and bright red to make us taste the cherries.
Plant a seed at home and keep a diary of its growth.

problem.en: What lesson does Grandfather give about luck?

text.en: Rakesh wants to keep the seed because it is lucky.
Grandfather says nothing is lucky if put away.
He should plant it and care for it.

prompt.en: Why does Rakesh plant the seed in a shady corner?

points.en: Rakesh plants a cherry seed on his grandfather's advice.
Nothing is lucky if put away; use it.
The story is about patience, care and nature.
